proposals.before: Zhiyi’s son, born Chixin, succeeded him.
proposals.after: When Zhiyi died, his son was named Chixin.
proposals.reason: Chinese records Zhiyi died and that his son was named Chixin; it does not say born or that the son succeeded.

proposals.before: In the fourth year Keyong led fifty thousand men to save Chenzhou, marched out by Tianjing Pass, and sought a road through Heyang. Ge Zhuang barred the way, so he forded the Yellow River from Hezhong.
proposals.after: In the fourth year Keyong led fifty thousand men to save Chenzhou, marched out by Tianjing Pass, and sought a road through Heyang. Zhuge Shuang barred the way, so he forded the Yellow River from Hezhong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 诸葛爽 is the surname Zhuge plus given name Shuang, not Ge Zhuang.

proposals.before: That night, after the drinking ended, Keyong fell asleep in his cups. Quanzhong’s men attacked and set the lodge ablaze. Attendant Guo Jingquan snuffed the lamps, pulled Keyong under the bed, dashed water on his face, and warned him of the ambush.
proposals.after: That night, after the drinking ended, Keyong fell asleep in his cups. Quanzhong’s men attacked and set the lodge ablaze. Attendant Guo Jingzhu snuffed the lamps, pulled Keyong under the bed, dashed water on his face, and warned him of the ambush.
proposals.reason: Chinese 郭景铢 is Guo Jingzhu; 铢 is not read quan.

proposals.before: In Guangqi 1 (885) Wang Chongrong of Hezhong clashed with the eunuch Tian Lingzi. Chongrong was ordered to Yanzhou and Wang Chuncun of Dingzhou was named military governor of Hezhong; Keyong was told to march troops escorting Chuncun into the circuit.
proposals.after: In Guangqi 1 (885) Wang Chongrong of Hezhong clashed with the eunuch Tian Lingzi. Chongrong was ordered to Yanzhou and Wang Chucun of Dingzhou was named military governor of Hezhong; Keyong was told to march troops escorting Chucun into the circuit.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王处存 is Wang Chucun; 处 is Chu, not Chun.

proposals.before: Yao was Gong’s brother and had backed his claim.
proposals.after: Yao was Gong’s younger brother and had aided Gong in the struggle.
proposals.reason: Chinese 弟 is specifically younger brother; literal already has younger brother, and 助珙 is aid to Gong rather than a generic claim.

proposals.before: Keyong camped for a month without moving. Zhaozong sent Princes Jiepi of Yan and Yun of Dan to address him as an elder kinsman and beg him to act.
proposals.after: Keyong camped for more than a month without advancing. Zhaozong sent the Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the Prince of Dan, Yun, to treat him as an elder brother and plead for urgent aid.
proposals.reason: Chinese is 留月余不进 and 延王戒丕、丹王允兄事克用; idiomatic drops 余, fuses the two princely titles, and weakens 兄事 / 告急.

proposals.before: In the fourth month Shi Shuzong came in through Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing through Xinkou, Ge Congzhou through Tumen, Wang Churen through Feihu, and Hou Yan through Yindi.
proposals.after: In the fourth month Shi Shuzong came in through Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing through Xinkou, Ge Congzhou through Tumen, Wang Chuzhi through Feihu, and Hou Yan through Yindi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王处直 is Wang Chuzhi; the idiomatic spelling Wang Churen misreads 直.

proposals.before: Keyong held that Liang had dragged the emperor west by force, that Tianyou was no true Tang era, and refused to use it—he still dated events to Tianfu.
proposals.after: Keyong held that Liang had coerced the emperor into moving the capital, that Tianyou was no true Tang era, and refused to use it—he still dated events to Tianfu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劫天子以迁都 states coercion and a capital move, not a westward dragging; Luoyang is not west of the old capital.

decisions.after: Zhiyi died. His son was called Chixin.
decisions.reason: 执宜死 explicitly reports Zhiyi's death, and 其子曰赤心 identifies his son as Chixin. The original invents both birth wording and a succession that the sentence does not state.
诸葛 is the compound surname Zhuge and 爽 is Shuang. Ge Zhuang is a false segmentation and reading of the same three characters.
郭景铢 is Guo Jingzhu: 铢 is read zhu, not quan. The replacement corrects the attendant's personal name without changing the event.
王处存 is Wang Chucun; 处 is read Chu in this name. Chuncun inserts a nonexistent n and recurs in the following narrative.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以定州王处存为河中节度使

decisions.reason: 弟 specifies that Yao was Gong's younger brother, and 助珙以争 says he aided Gong in the struggle. The proposal restores both details.
月余 means more than a month. 延王戒丕 and 丹王允 are two separately titled princes, and 兄事克用 means they treated Keyong as an elder brother while urgently appealing for help.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 留月余不进，昭宗遣延王戒丕、丹王允兄事克用，且告急

decisions.reason: 王处直 is Wang Chuzhi; 直 is zhi, not ren. The proposed correction matches the Chinese and the supplied pinyin.
劫天子以迁都 means coercing the emperor to move the capital. The original adds an incorrect westward direction even though the move described in s0134 was to Luoyang.

claimRetractions.reason: Ge Zhuang is only a mistranslation of 诸葛爽, while a correct Zhuge Shuang name claim already exists for this person, so the false duplicate alias must be removed.

claimRevisions.reason: The structured personal-name claim must follow the accepted correction of 铢 from quan to zhu.
The personal-name claim repeats the Chuncun misspelling corrected in the translation and must read Wang Chucun.
The given-name claim has the same inserted n as the bad full-name spelling and must be corrected to Chucun across both cited units.
The normalized action label embeds the misspelled name and must match the corrected Wang Chucun identity.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 诏克用以兵护处存之镇

claimRevisions.reason: The structured name already supplies the correct pinyin Chuzhi, so its English spelling must not retain the mistranslated Churen.
